text:
maya: heads-up: hitting a weird SSE parsing edge in sampleapp-js. after a quick reconnect the keepalive ":" line sometimes ends up concatenated with the next JSON data event, so client tries to parse a bad payload and throws. Seen on local + staging behind our edge proxy. :thinking:

alex: which SDK/version? sampleapp or your app?

maya: sampleapp-js (master + latest sdk@0.9.3). minimal repro in sampleapp -> start, kill network for ~200ms, restore. sometimes you get a chunk like:

```
: keepalive\ndata: {"id":"msg_123","text":"hello"}\n\n
```

but other times we get this merged on one line from the client perspective (after reconnect/stream resume):

```
: keepalive\ndata: {"id":"msg_123","text":"hello"}\n: keepalive\ndata: {"id":"msg_124","text":"next"}
```

which is fine. the bug is when the keepalive delimiter and data line get split/merged so event parsing sees something like:

```
: keepalive\ndata: {"id":"msg_123","text":"hello"}\n\r\n{"id":"msg_124","text":"next"}\n\n
```

-- so the leading `{` of the next JSON arrives on the same buffer boundary that the client treats as a data continuation and ends up as `\n{"id":...` appended to previous buffer and then JSON.parse fails.

ryan: hmm, sounds like chunk boundary/CRLF normalization at the proxy layer. my hunch: when fetch is aborted+re-issued (auth refresh path), some middle proxy concatenates the tail of previous chunk with head of new chunk without the expected separator. nginx's `proxy_buffering` and some http/1.1 keepalive edgecases can do this. Also check if TLS terminator rewrites newlines.

alex: can you paste the raw bytes (hexdump) or curl -v -N output? also are you using EventSource polyfill or our fetch-based SSE?

maya: here's trimmed curl session from staging (with replaced tokens):

```
$ curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" "https://staging.redwood.io/stream/.."
> GET /stream/.. HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: text/event-stream
< Transfer-Encoding: chunked
<
: keepalive\n\ndata: {"id":"a","t":1}\n\n\r\n{"id":"b","t":2}\n\n
```

looks like `\r\n` gets inserted between chunks occasionally. client parser expects `\n\n` event delimiter.

sam: related note — our js-sdk parse loop is pretty naive: it looks for `\n\n` then splits by `\n` and consumes lines. if intermediate `\r` appears out of place it can leave stray `\r` at buffer start which confuses JSON parsing. I can try a small fix: normalize all `\r\n` -> `\n`, treat leading `:` lines as separate keepalive events (ignore them), and only attempt JSON.parse on lines that start with `data:` after trimming. pseudocode:

```
buffer = buffer.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n")
for line in buffer.split("\n"):
  if line.startsWith(":"):
    // keepalive, ignore
    continue
  if line.startsWith("data:"):
    data_buf += line.slice(5).trim() + "\n"
  if line == "":
    emit(data_buf)
    data_buf = ""
```

alex: that helps. but we should also harden resume/token-refresh path: when auth refresh aborts fetch, the SDK should discard any partial buffer (or mark partial and re-request with last-event-id). otherwise we try to merge partial data from aborted stream into new one.

maya: i tried a patch that normalizes CRLF and throws away a partial buffer on abort. seems to cut down the failure rate from ~8% to <1% in my quick loop. still seeing rare failure when network flaps super fast (20-50ms) during auth refresh.

ryan: let's also inspect our edge (the staging ELB + nginx) config for `proxy_http_version` and `proxy_buffering off` for streaming endpoints. if edge coalesces small buffers to reduce packets it can mask SSE framing. I can spin up a proxy with `proxy_buffering off; chunked_transfer_encoding off;` to reproduce.

sam: i'll open a js-sdk PR with the buffer normalization + discard-on-abort + unit tests that simulate reconnect + interleaved keepalives. will add a flaky e2e in sampleapp that does repeated auth refresh (short TTL token).

alex: please include a short note about impacting customers (P2?) — if parse error leads to thrown exceptions, apps can crash if they don't guard. mark issue and link PR.

ci-bot: build passed for branch fix/sse-buffer-normalize (CI: 12/12 checks) :white_check_mark:

maya: thanks all — assigning to @sam for PR and @ryan to check edge config. filing followup to consider server-side safe separators (e.g., explicit event `id` sync on reconnect).

alex: nice triage. after PR we'll backport to the 0.9.x patch release and add a small note in changelog and sampleapp README about unstable networks.

maya: leaving logs and minimal repro in the thread's gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/devex-sse-repro (private).
